audit.why: Mirror explicitly left diff EVEN and diffRating 6/10, and 50.42% over 357 games agrees. Early belongs to Poppy while Illaoi is immobile and tentacle-less, level 6 is Poppy's on the Keeper's Verdict fling, and the tentacle field takes over as it thickens.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 read Skill, Level 2 read Illaoi and Level 6 read Skill, all three against the mirror, the packet chart and the page's own whys.
audit.why: whys[0] says she cannot punish you at 1, whys[1] says Q+E stuns an escape-less Illaoi before her field is online, whys[4] says the R fling removes her entire power source. Mirror point 3 flipped rows 0, 1 and 4 to Poppy and the packet chart agrees on all three. Rows 3 and 6 are a genuine three-way conflict and are deliberately left alone — see questionsForUser.
audit.corrected: phases[0,1,4].side and win[0,1,4] flipped to Poppy as one group, rated 6/10, 6/10 and 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was buried under boilerplate: 'W any dash he tries — his mobility is a suggestion'. Harsh Lesson genuinely is a dash and Steadfast Presence genuinely does stop it — but Harsh Lesson is a 4-second cooldown against W's 20 seconds at rank 1, so it is not a suggestion, it is a trade you get to make once per five of hers.
audit.why: The mirror named this the decisive interaction of the lane from the other side. Stating it without the cooldown gap teaches the player to hold W for a dash that is already back.
audit.corrected: Both cooldowns stated in dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[2].d, phases[1].why and breakdown.cooldowns; Test of Spirit given its 16/15/14/13/12s and 900 range everywhere it is named.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's first defect is 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere — needs concrete wait for X before you Y lines'. Correct: not one field told the player what to wait for.
audit.why: The sequence that wins the lane is: sidestep or wait out Test of Spirit (16s), then step in; W only for the Harsh Lesson leap; Keeper's Verdict only after Test of Spirit is spent.
audit.corrected: Sequencing written into tradeGood, dosFull[0].d, phases[4].why, breakdown.mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] mentions anti-heal generically, but no lane field said why or when.
audit.why: Prophet of an Elder God heals Illaoi whenever a tentacle damages a champion, so every slam that lands on you is sustain. Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid claimed 'W's slow helps you walk out' after Test of Spirit lands. Steadfast Presence does not slow the enemy on activation — it grants Poppy Move Speed, and only applies a slow and grounding to a dash it actually stops.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit about which effect comes from which trigger, and the mirror agent corrected the same confusion from the other side.
audit.corrected: mid now credits the move speed, which is the effect that actually gets you out of the field.

edits.before: - Illaoi Test of Spirit: matchup-defining — Her vessel pull. Sidestep it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.after: Trade strictly around Test of Spirit (16s): when it is spent, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve her.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even out as her tentacle field thickens and her flat sustain starts eating your trades, so pick your spots — only all-in when tentacles are sparse. Level 6 is your real edge: Keeper's Verdict (R) flings her completely out of her tentacle field, stripping every bit of her power for the fight, or peels her off you if she dives. The whole game is fighting on YOUR ground, never hers; if she E's you (Test of Spirit), W's slow helps you walk out instead of dying in the field.

notes: The packet's suspectName on wants.foe[0] ('Land Test of Spirit') is a FALSE POSITIVE — that is the correct ability name; the near-miss distance comes from the leading verb, exactly as the mirror agent found on its own side. Left unasserted: champ-data/_kits/illaoi.json gives Leap of Faith an 'untargetable' derived flag and _missing-interactions repeats it as 'Illaoi can go untargetable through your commit'. Riot's own description is 'Illaoi smashes her idol into the ground, dealing physical damage to nearby enemies. A Tentacle spawns for each enemy champion hit' — no untargetability anywhere in it. I did not write that advice and I did not write its negation either. Gendered boilerplate still reading 'him/his' for Illaoi survives in breakdown.trading, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, report[3].t, report[8].t, report[9].t and report[12].t; those are concatenations of fields fixed here, so they should regenerate, but if they are stored independently they need the same pass.
